results.question: Write a Prometheus alerting rule named BatteryLowOnBattery that fires immediately when gpulab_battery_capacity_percent is below 20 and gpulab_ac_online is 0 on the same node.

run.final:
# Prometheus Alerting Rule

Here's a Prometheus alerting rule that fires immediately when both conditions are met on the same node:

```yaml
groups:
  - name: battery_alerts
    interval: 30s
    rules:
      - alert: BatteryLowOnBattery
        expr: |
          gpulab_battery_capacity_percent < 20 and
          gpulab_ac_online == 0
        for: 0s
        labels:
          severity: critical
        annotations:
          summary: "Battery is low and not connected to AC power"
          description: "Node {{ $labels.instance }} has a battery capacity of {{ $value }}% and is not connected to AC power."
```

## Explanation

| Property | Value | Description |
|----------|-------|-------------|
| **Alert Name** | `BatteryLowOnBattery` | The name of the alert |
| **Expression** | `gpulab_battery_capacity_percent < 20 and gpulab_ac_online == 0` | Both conditions must be true on the same node (Prometheus automatically matches by label) |
| **For** | `0s` | Fires **immediately** when the condition is met (set to `1m` or longer if you want to avoid flapping) |
| **Severity** | `critical` | Alert severity level |
| **Annotations** | Summary & Description | Human-readable information for the alert |

## Notes

- The `for: 0s` setting ensures the alert fires immediately when both conditions are satisfied
- If you want to avoid flapping (alerts firing and clearing repeatedly), set `for: 1m` or longer
- The `{{ $labels.instance }}` and `{{ $value }}` variables will be populated with the node name and battery capacity percentage, respectively
- This rule will match all nodes that expose the `gpulab_battery_capacity_percent` and `gpulab_ac_online` metrics

# Prometheus Alerting Rule: DataDiskAlmostFull

Here's a Prometheus alerting rule that monitors the `/data` mountpoint for low disk space:

```yaml
groups:
  - name: disk_alerts
    interval: 1m
    rules:
      - alert: DataDiskAlmostFull
        expr: |
          (node_filesystem_avail_bytes{mountpoint="/data"} / node_filesystem_size_bytes{mountpoint="/data"}) < 0.1
        for: 5m
        labels:
          severity: warning
        annotations:
          summary: "Data disk almost full"
          description: "The /data filesystem is running low on disk space. Only {{ $value | humanizePercentage }} available."
          runbook_url: "https://your-org.com/runbooks/data-disk-almost-full"
```

## Explanation

| Component | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| **Metric** | `node_filesystem_avail_bytes` and `node_filesystem_size_bytes` |
| **Label Filter** | `{mountpoint="/data"}` - targets only the `/data` mountpoint |
| **Expression** | Calculates available space ratio (`available / total`) |
| **Threshold** | `< 0.1` (10% free space) |
| **Duration** | `5m` - fires only after 5 minutes of sustained condition |

results.question: Write a Prometheus alerting rule named GPUThrottling that fires when gpulab_gpu_throttle_active is 1 for 3 minutes.

run.final:
# Prometheus Alerting Rule: GPUThrottling

## YAML Format

```yaml
groups:
  - name: gpu_alerts
    interval: 15s
    rules:
      - alert: GPUThrottling
        expr: gpulab_gpu_throttle_active == 1
        for: 3m
        labels:
          severity: critical
          team: gpu
        annotations:
          summary: "GPU throttling is active"
          description: "GPU throttling has been active for more than 3 minutes. This may indicate thermal or power delivery issues."
          runbook_url: "https://your-runbook-url.com/gpu-throttling"
```

## Raw PromQL Expression

```promql
gpulab_gpu_throttle_active == 1 for 3m
```

## Explanation

| Field | Value | Description |
|-------|-------|-------------|
| **Alert Name** | `GPUThrottling` | Name of the alert |
| **Metric** | `gpulab_gpu_throttle_active == 1` | Checks if the throttle status is active (value = 1) |
| **For Duration** | `3m` | The condition must persist for 3 minutes before firing |
| **Severity** | `critical` | Default severity level (can be adjusted) |

## How It Works

1. The rule monitors the `gpulab_gpu_throttle_active` metric
2. It only fires when the value is exactly `1` (active throttling)
3. The `for: 3m` clause ensures the alert only fires after the condition has been true for 3 minutes (reduces false positives from transient spikes)
4. The alert can be configured with labels (severity, team) and annotations (summary, description, runbook URL) for better alert management

## Example Alert Output

When this alert fires, Prometheus will display:

```
ALERTS{alertname="GPUThrottling",instance="gpu-node-01:9100",job="gpulab",severity="critical"}
  {description="GPU throttling has been active for more than 3 minutes. This may indicate thermal or power delivery issues.",summary="GPU throttling is active"}
  1704067200.000
```

## Additional Options

If you want to include the instance or node information in the alert, you can modify the expression:

```promql
gpulab_gpu_throttle_active == 1 for 3m
```

Or if you want to alert on any throttling (value of 1 or 2, for example):

```promql
gpulab_gpu_throttle_active > 0 for 3m
```

```yaml
          category: gpu
```


The `for` clause is optional and was omitted here since you specified "fires as soon as" the condition is met.

results.question: Write a Prometheus alerting rule named ScrapeFlapping that fires as soon as any target's up metric has changed value more than 3 times in the last 10 minutes.

run.final:
# Prometheus Alerting Rule: ScrapeFlapping

Here's the alerting rule that fires when any target's `up` metric changes value more than 3 times in the last 10 minutes:

```yaml
groups:
  - name: scrape_flapping
    interval: 1m
    rules:
      - alert: ScrapeFlapping
        expr: changes(up[10m]) > 3
        for: 0s
        labels:
          severity: warning
        annotations:
          summary: "Target {{ $labels.job }}/{{ $labels.instance }} is flapping"
          description: "The 'up' metric for target {{ $labels.job }}/{{ $labels.instance }} has changed value more than 3 times in the last 10 minutes."
```

## Explanation

| Component | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `changes(up[10m])` | Counts the number of times the `up` metric has changed value over the last 10 minutes |
| `> 3` | Triggers the alert when there are more than 3 changes |
| `for: 0s` | Fires immediately (no waiting period) when the condition is met |

## How It Works

- The `changes()` function tracks transitions between different values of the `up` metric
- Each time a target goes from `up=1` to `up=0` or vice versa, it counts as one change
- 3 changes could represent a pattern like: `up=1 → up=0 → up=1 → up=0` (or similar)
- The `or` function (implicit in Prometheus) ensures the alert fires if **any** target meets the condition

## Alternative (More Explicit)

If you want to be more explicit about firing for any target:

```yaml
      - alert: ScrapeFlapping
        expr: or(changes(up[10m]) > 3)
        for: 0s
```

Or using `vector(1)` to convert the boolean to a vector:

```yaml
      - alert: ScrapeFlapping
        expr: vector(1) and changes(up[10m]) > 3
        for: 0s
```

results.question: Write a Prometheus alerting rule named TargetDown that fires when any scrape target's up metric has been 0 for 2 minutes.

run.final:
# Prometheus Alerting Rule: TargetDown

Here's a Prometheus alerting rule that fires when any scrape target's `up` metric has been 0 for 2 minutes:

```yaml
groups:
  - name: target_down_alerts
    interval: 15s
    rules:
      - alert: TargetDown
        expr: up == 0
        for: 2m
        labels:
          severity: critical
        annotations:
          summary: "Target {{ $labels.instance }} is down"
          description: "Target {{ $labels.instance }} ({{ $labels.job }}) has been down for more than 2 minutes."
          runbook_url: "https://example.com/runbooks/target-down"
```

## Explanation

| Field | Value | Description |
|-------|-------|-------------|
| **alert** | `TargetDown` | Name of the alert |
| **expr** | `up == 0` | The condition that triggers the alert (target is not up) |
| **for** | `2m` | The duration the condition must persist before firing |
| **severity** | `critical` | Alert severity level |
| **annotations** | - | Human-readable description and summary |

## How It Works

- The `up` metric is a built-in Prometheus metric that indicates whether a target is up (`1`) or down (`0`)
- The rule monitors all targets across all jobs
- The `for: 2m` clause ensures the alert only fires after the target has been down for 2 continuous minutes (prevents false positives from transient network blips)
- When the alert fires, it includes the `instance` and `job` labels in the summary for easy identification

## Example Alert Output

When this alert fires, you'll see something like:

```
TargetDown: 1
  - instance: "server1.example.com:9090"
  - job: "node"
  - severity: critical
  - summary: "Target server1.example.com:9090 is down"
  - description: "Target server1.example.com:9090 (node) has been down for more than 2 minutes."
```

## Additional Options

If you want to alert on specific targets or jobs, you can add a `matchers` clause:

```yaml
      - alert: TargetDown
        expr: up == 0
        for: 2m
        matchers:
          - job: "node"
        labels:
          severity: critical
        annotations:
          summary: "Node target {{ $labels.instance }} is down"
```

Or alert only on targets that were previously up:

```yaml
      - alert: TargetDown
        expr: up == 0
        for: 2m
        labels:
          severity: critical
        annotations:
          summary: "Target {{ $labels.instance }} is down"
        # Only fire if the target was up at the last successful scrape
        # (requires a separate metric like up{job="..."} or similar)
```
